title: Repaying what we borrowed during my father's illness
story: When my father was ill last year we borrowed from three relatives to keep the household going and to pay for his medicines. Between them it comes to about 4,000 USD. They have never asked for it back and they would not, but my mother says it weighs on her every day and she wants it settled while she can. We still have the small plot outside town that has been in the family for two generations. My brother and I both work, though not steadily.
reviewerNote: Information requested. The debt is stated plainly and two facts our policy turns on are not. Whether the relatives are actually seeking repayment matters, and the copy says the opposite twice while also saying the family wants it settled, which is a real situation and not a contradiction to hold against anyone. Whether the household could meet it from what it holds matters as well, and the plot outside town is mentioned without a value or a statement of whether it can be sold. I asked both questions and said in the message that either answer is workable; what is not workable is a reviewer guessing on the organizer's behalf, which is what would have to happen to record a decision today.
